uncited: Category-Specific Learned Initialization uses meta-learning to capture shape and appearance priors from a large collection of objects within a specific category (e.g., cars on ShapeNet) to initialize the weights of instance-specific neural radiance field (NeRF) MLPs.
It solves the problem of poor reconstruction quality and slow convergence when training on novel scenes with sparse input views, where standard random initialization fails to complete partial views.

It sets itself apart from standard initialization by distilling category-level knowledge into the starting weights, allowing the model to generalize better and converge faster, particularly in data-sparse regimes.
- **Output:** A set of optimized MLP weights $\theta_{init}$ that serve as the initialization for instance-specific "thing" MLPs during novel scene reconstruction.
- $\theta$: The weights of the MLP (typically a "thing" MLP with 4 hidden layers and width 128, using positional encoding with $L=6$ frequencies for object coordinates).
- $D_k$: The dataset for client $k$, defined as a bundle of rays corresponding to every observed pixel of object instance $k$.
The method employs Federated Averaging (FedAvg) to meta-learn the initialization.
**Server Initialization:** Initialize global weights $\theta_0$.
Receive current weights $\theta_t$ from the server.
Split $D_k$ into batches of ray bundles of size $B$.
*(Note: $\eta$ is the learning rate, $\ell$ is the loss function, typically reconstruction loss.
Return the updated local weights $\theta_{t+1}^k$ to the server.
**Final Initialization:** The resulting $\theta_{final}$ is used as the initialization for the thing MLPs when training on a novel scene.
Initialize the MLP for each object instance track $T$ with the meta-learned weights $\theta_{final}$.
Train the inference-time scene representation network on the novel scene data, focusing only on the individual set of object instances present.
A decentralized federated training algorithm used to realize category-specific learned initialization for thing MLPs by meta-learning from 2D rendered images of 3D models from ShapeNet.
It allows for parallel processing of unique object instances.
It is chosen when a large shape collection is available for a specific category (e.g., cars and vans) to distill priors into initialization weights.
- **Time Complexity:** The meta-training phase requires $T$ outer epochs, each involving $K$ parallel client updates of $E$ inner epochs.
The total computational cost is proportional to $T \times K \times E$.
- **Memory Complexity:** Requires storing the MLP weights $\theta$ and the datasets $D_k$ for each client.
- **When to use:** When reconstructing scenes with sparse input views for categories with available prior data (e.g., cars, vans).
The method leverages meta-learning [11] to capture category-specific shape and appearance priors.
It uses the FedAvg algorithm [36], which is known to be equivalent to REPTILE [42] meta-learning [25].
The approach was evaluated on ShapeNet [5] cars (provided by [56]) and applied to cars and vans in dynamic KITTI scenes.
